value.hook: Before trusting script-marker statusline rates or sampled process names
value.title: Hook attribution across exec

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Hook attribution must survive exec, not just recognize a script name.

The existing spawn-rate sampler has a specific blind spot for the managed
Copilot statusline. It increments statusline_runs_seen_per_s only when a
newly observed PID's argv contains copilot-statusline-pij. The managed
script then execs pij-rs statusline copilot, so that marker disappears.
Moreover, the sampler inspects cur - seen: a PID first observed as a shell
is not inspected again when the same PID execs into pij-rs. Adding the
exec'd argv spelling alone therefore does not remove every miss.
The low reported rate is a sampling lower bound, not a render count,
even though that field's name lacks the lower_bound suffix.

Source: harness/scripts/spawn-rate.py:109-147 and
harness/scripts/copilot-statusline-pij.sh. During #240's live host
observation, the same child PIDs changed from shell names to pij-rs while
retaining the registered Copilot as their direct parent. These are exec
phases, not one process allocation per observed name. Conversely, do not
infer recursive daemon CLI launches from a transient sampled child comm:
the per-operation daemon counters describe what the launcher requested,
while the process sampler describes the name it caught at one instant.

Keep the evidence surfaces separate: daemon spawn counters exclude the
Copilot-owned statusline process; script-marker sampling can miss its exec
phase; exact-host parent-link observations can establish the observed
topology without collecting argv or environments, but names alone do not
identify every command or prove every CLI distribution's launch contract.

magicWand: add an exec-transition fixture to the existing sampler, recognize
both the managed-script and pij-rs statusline copilot forms, and explicitly
label the resulting statusline reading as a lower bound. If attribution
revisits newly seen PIDs, give that reclassification an explicit lifetime;
do not turn this into an unbounded per-process poll or claim sampling is an
exact invocation counter. This is a follow-up, not a retroactive merge gate.

Evidence: #240, merge 2d5b1a9c19c0c771a43a4ef46f87a54398e2608c,
PR comment 6968528883 and AFTER output
dfc13d5526ed0db92bf1f58a96b050d9791faeae. The comment holds the measured
before/after receipts and their attribution limits. This note adds the
exec-specific sensor gap; it does not replace the role's existing
"Price renderers per draw, not per turn" or "CPU attribution and profile
limits" guidance.
